newsitem.title: USA: EEOC to monitor Texaco discrimination compliance.
newsitem.headline: EEOC to monitor Texaco discrimination compliance.

text.p: The Equal Employment Opportunity Commission said Friday it reached an agreement with Texaco Inc. to intervene in a racial discrimination case the company agreed to settle in November.

Texaco agreed on Nov. 15 to pay $176.1 million to settle a lawsuit filed by black employees who claimed they were discriminated against in pay and promotions. The plaintiffs said it was the biggest settlement in a race discrimination case in the United States.

The commission was troubled that it had been excluded from the settlement talks and has been negotiating with Texaco to monitor the settlement, which included plans to establish an "equality and tolerance" task force. The talks have delayed final settlement of the discrimination case.

Under the agreement presented to a federal judge here, the commission can monitor Texaco's compliance with federal law by inspecting Texaco's premises and records and interviewing current or former employees.
In addition, Texaco must give the agency a report on its plans for promotions and in coming years information about vacancies filled by promotion.
A Texaco spokesman said the company was satisfied with the agreement and said the EEOC's intervention was not seen as intrusive.

As part of the settlement, White Plains, N.Y.-based Texaco released a plan last month to boost employment, career development and recruiting of minorities, as well as increasing purchasing from minority- and women-owned companies.
The plan was well-received by lawyers representing the black plaintiffs and the Rev. Jesse Jackson, who responded by calling for an end to a consumer boycott of Texaco he helped initiate in November.
At Friday's hearing, U.S. District Judge Charles Brieant set a hearing for Feb. 27 to consider the settlement.

Daniel Berger, a lawyer for the plaintiffs, told the judge he will submit the formal settlement agreement by next Friday. He said other possible members of the class action will be notified by Jan. 17 and that those who object or wish to opt out must notify the court by Feb. 20.

Problems at Texaco surfaced after plaintiffs' lawyers in the discrimination lawsuit received secret tapes of senior executives discussing the destruction of damaging documents. The executives allegedly also made racist remarks.
